Austin Film Festival Announces 2026 Script and Film Competition Award Winners

Overview of the 33rd Annual Austin Film Festival

The 33rd annual Austin Film Festival (AFF) has concluded its 2026 edition by announcing the winners across its various script and film competition categories. Following a submission process that received over 12,500 entries, 78 projects were selected for the finalist round. From this pool, 21 writers and writing teams were honored during an Awards Luncheon held in Austin, Texas.

Barbara Morgan, Executive Director of the Austin Film Festival, stated that the organization intends to provide more than just awards to participants. According to Morgan, the goal is to foster industry relationships and offer professional development opportunities to emerging storytellers.

Competition Structure and Industry Impact

A panel comprised of industry professionals—including creators and writers with credits on projects such as *The Bear*, *Succession*, and *Parks and Rec*—evaluated the submissions. The festival aims to connect finalists with managers, agents, and producers through resources like the Producers Book and the annual Writers Conference.

Key details regarding the competition outcomes include:

  • Industry Access: Many winners receive fellowship opportunities designed to provide mentorship and career guidance.
  • Academy Consideration: Select winners in narrative, documentary, and animated short categories may be eligible for Academy Award consideration.
  • Diverse Categories: Awards were distributed across a wide range of formats, including drama features, teleplay pilots, fiction podcasts, and digital series.

Notable Award Recipients

The festival recognized projects across two main divisions: Script Competition and Film Competition. Among the honored script works were:

  • Drama Feature: *Sisters* by Zenas Cao
  • Comedy Feature: *Pure Intentions* by Sarah Peele
  • Horror Feature: *Dyscopia* by Bobby Marino
  • Sci-Fi Feature: *Louis and Puck* by Parker Rawlins and William Cowser

In the film competition, notable winners included:

  • Narrative Feature: *Sweet Milk Lake*, directed by Harvey Zielinski
  • Documentary Feature: *Strange Ashes: The Untold Story of Elisabeth Elliot*, directed by Laura Waters Hinson
  • Narrative Short: *Paper Plane*, directed by Saoirse Ronan

For a complete list of all winners and to verify specific fellowship details, attendees and interested parties can visit the official Austin Film Festival website.
